title: A Verdict for the Cipher
premise: Mara Amberdale, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, receives a confession letter for a hit-and-run closed a year ago—the postmark dated the day after the victim's funeral. As Mara reopens the case in secret, he discovers the confessed driver is dead, the letter was typed by someone else, and the town's beloved judge orchestrated both the accident and its cover-up. Racing a statute-of-limitations deadline and threats against his own life, Mara must choose between handing evidence to the corrupt system or exposing it himself; in the end, he publishes the truth anonymously, finds belonging among the victim's family who take him in, and chooses love—his growing bond with the victim's sister—over the duty of staying invisible.
about_author: Astrid Zhou is a former claims adjuster from coastal Oregon who spent a decade reading other people's misfortunes on paper before writing her own. She writes mysteries about ordinary people who refuse to look away.

chapters.title: Postmarked Grief
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A year after closing the Halloway hit-and-run file, Mara receives a typed confession postmarked the day after the funeral—signed by a man already dead. He tells no one, telling himself it's a prank, but his memory keeps replaying details that don't match the official record. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: The File That Won't Stay Shut
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Pulling the archived case at night, Mara notices discrepancies only he would catch: tire marks photographed but never measured, a witness statement with a subtly altered phrase. He visits the victim's widow under a false pretext and glimpses her daughter, Iris, who recognizes something honest in him. Beat: the pull between detachment and involvement begins.

chapters.title: A Dead Man's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Iris, a forensic document examiner, is asked by an anonymous client to authenticate the confession letter and realizes the typewriter belongs to the county courthouse. She doesn't know her anonymous client is the investigator sniffing around her father's death. Beat: two investigations converge without their owners knowing.

chapters.title: The Judge's Benefactors
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following the money, Mara finds the settlement was paid by a foundation chaired by Judge Ellery Voss, the town's moral pillar, whose protégé Daniel Crewe was the driver who died—officially of an accident. Mara realizes the confession letter is bait, meant to draw out whoever still doubts. Beat: dread replaces curiosity.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Iris confronts her mother about the night of the crash and learns her mother saw the car—and was paid to forget. Shattered, Iris nearly burns the authentication report, but instead mails a copy to the one address she trusts: the anonymous client. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Letter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mara and Iris finally meet when she traces the client address to his office; recognition is instant and volatile—he lied to her, she's been investigating him. They pool what they know over a long night: Voss covered for Crewe, then killed him when his conscience surfaced. Beat: distrust hardening into partnership, and something warmer.

chapters.title: The Statute's Edge
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Voss's people break into Mara's office and steal the original letter; his license is suspended on fabricated misconduct charges. With eleven days until the civil claim expires and every legal door slamming shut, Mara understands justice will not come through the law. Beat: loss of everything safe, clarity gained.

chapters.title: Crewe's Last Night
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Tracking Crewe's final hours, Iris finds his hidden recorder in a boathouse—audio of Voss ordering the cover-up and admitting the crash was Crewe driving drunk while Voss watched from the passenger seat. The recording also names the witness payments. Beat: triumph shadowed by horror at how deep it goes.

chapters.title: Verdict Without a Court
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the courthouse centennial ceremony, Mara and Iris broadcast the recording to the assembled town as Voss takes the stage. Confronted publicly, Voss breaks—first bluster, then confession—as deputies who owe him nothing anymore arrest him. Beat: the climax; catharsis earned outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: A Place at the Table
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Months later, Mara testifies freely, declines a prestigious offer requiring silence, and is set a place at the Halloway family table—no longer invisible, no longer alone. He closes the case not in a file but in a promise to Iris. Beat: belonging won, love chosen over duty, quiet peace.
